newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand moves to restore confidence in finance sector.
newsitem.headline: Thailand moves to restore confidence in finance sector.

text.p: Thai authorities, in a move to restore confidence in the country's troubled finance sector, on Monday appealed for calm in the market and announced steps aimed at preventing sudden finance firm collapses.

"I would like to assure people that the government is closely monitoring and keep situation under control and there is no cause for concern. People should stop and think before (growing panicky)," Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh said.
Central bank governor Rerngchai Marakanond ordered banks and finance firms to raise provisions for sub-standard assets and asked 10 finance firms to boost capital immediately.
Rerngchai also told a news conference that a fund run by the Bank of Thailand was prepared to help these firms raise capital if requested and it will participate in their future management.
"Their capital hikes would help assure creditors of these firms that they can continue to operate soundly," he said.

Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan told the news conference that the Thai government, banks and finance firms would go all out to help ease a domestic liquidity crunch faced by the local financial sector. He also appealed for market calm while measures were being taken to help the troubled sector.

Permanent secretary for finance Chatumongkol Sonakul said the 10 finance firms were ordered to raise capital because they did not have sufficient provisions for doubtful loans and sub-standard assets and they faced short-term cashflow problems.

Rerngchai said the central bank fund would open an 8.25 billion baht credit line for these firms until end-1997 and other companies outside the 10 firms mentioned could also seek assistance from the authorities.
Three of the 10 firms are listed on the Thai bourse - International Trust and Finance Plc, Dynamic Eastern Finance Thailand (1991) Plc, and Sri Dhana Finance and Securities Plc.
Thailand's stock exchange said it had suspended trading in all banks and finance and securities company shares until further notice.
The bourse halted trading in the two sectors in the morning session pending the announcement by the central bank and finance ministry.
Thai stocks fell 2.51 percent by lunch on Monday amid poor market sentiment.
